design.primary_estimand: standardized joint dependence minus standardized exact-context dependence, where standardized dependence is covariance divided by p (1 - p)
design.primary_statistic: ordinary least squares slope on log2(batch size) inside each cell, then the equal-weight mean over the 4 analyzed cells
design.uncertainty: cluster bootstrap over size-32 super-groups within cell and assignment

historical_size_16_b3.scale: raw joint-minus-exact covariance from the sealed A9 analysis
historical_size_16_b3.use: descriptive comparison only; the sealed A9 result used the earlier output contract and is never pooled into this experiment

interpretations.flat_positive: per-size contrasts are above the practical contrast at every size and the slope interval contains zero and excludes the practical slope: batching introduces dependence, but dependence does not materially grow with size
interpretations.inconclusive: the slope interval is wider than twice the practical slope or a cell slope interval is wider than four times it: the experiment is inconclusive, and the absence of significance is not evidence of equivalence
interpretations.non_monotonic: the per-size contrasts are not ordered in size and the slope interval contains zero while some per-size intervals exclude it: dependence varies with size without a simple dose response
interpretations.null: every per-size contrast interval contains zero and lies below the practical contrast: the earlier size-16 effect does not replicate under the uniform contract
interpretations.positive_monotonic: the cross-family slope interval lies wholly above zero and every cell slope is positive: pairwise error dependence strengthens with batch size
interpretations.threshold: contrasts at the two smallest sizes lie below the practical contrast and at least the largest size lies above it: evidence for a practical batch-size boundary

outcome.note: these labels are descriptive readings of the frozen thresholds; success is not defined as a positive slope, and an inconclusive label never becomes an equivalence claim
